audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Tryndamere levels 3 and 4-5 and gave Renekton levels 1 and 6, while the whys directly beneath said the opposite on four of those rows.
audit.why: The already-audited mirror set levels 2 and 3 to Renekton, and levels 4-5, level 6 and first item to Skill. Renekton's edge is the fury window at 2-3; by 4-5 his fury empties between trades and Bloodlust pays the chip back, and both ultimates are 120/100/80s, so 6 is whoever spends first.
audit.corrected: Skill, Renekton, Renekton, Skill, Skill, Skill, Tryndamere with ratings 5,3,3,5,5,5,7 — the inverse of the mirror's — in matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] built the first-item spike around 'Battle Fury crit chance', and difficulty read 7.5/10 with a 'Tricky matchup' footer in a lane Tryndamere wins 53.12% of 1666 games.
audit.why: Battle Fury is not a current item name, and the mirror puts first item at Skill rather than a Tryndamere takeover — the takeover is two items. Undying Rage and Dominus share a 120/100/80s cooldown, which is the real content of the level-6 row.
audit.corrected: First item reframed as even with Ruthless Predator's 16/14/12/10/8s named; the takeover moved to two items; difficulty set to 5/10 to match the win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said 'Empowered = long stun' but never gave either duration, never mentioned that the empowered W destroys damage shields, and never named the auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Riot's text: Ruthless Predator stuns 0.75 seconds, or three slashes for 1.5 seconds above 50 Fury, and the empowered version destroys damage shields on the target. It is also an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up — not the cast — is the cue to step back. Watching his fury bar tells you which version is coming; watching the cooldown does not.
audit.corrected: Both durations, the shield destruction and the reset written into spikes[0], phases[1].why and phases[0].why.

audit.why: missingInteractions flags 'needs-antiheal' — Cull the Meek heals him for a portion of damage dealt on a 7s cooldown, and report[8] already calls for Executioner's Calling early.
audit.corrected: Reinforced in phases[3].why so the anti-heal timing is tied to a level rather than left in the item list.

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Renekton contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Neither of you commits at 1. Watch his fury bar rather than his cooldowns — every button he holds grows above 50 Fury.

edits.before: E lets you spin in and out of exchanges on your terms. Only take the trade when Renekton's Ruthless Predator is down.
edits.after: Ruthless Predator stuns 0.75s, or 1.5s above 50 Fury, and it resets his auto — the wind-up is your cue to step back.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Renekton must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: His W into Q and E out-damages anything you hold at 3, and Cull the Meek heals him back. Concede it and farm the wave.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Ruthless Predator's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Even now: his fury empties between trades, so punish that gap. Grievous Wounds early — Cull the Meek heals him through your chip.

edits.before: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds — dives and coin-flip all-ins become yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Renekton's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Undying Rage makes you unkillable for 5 seconds on 120/100/80s, and Dominus runs the same 120/100/80s — level 6 goes to whoever spends it second, so make him spend first.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Ruthless Predator's cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker is your spike, but his empowered W still opens — force fights once that stun is spent.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Ruthless Predator and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane is decided by how well you read his fury bar and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7.5/10, Renekton carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 5/10, Renekton carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: Level 4-5 favours Renekton — his fury-fueled trades and E resets keep him ahead in the kill window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out — his fury drains between trades while Bloodlust heals the chip back off.

edits.before: First item favours Tryndamere — crit and lifesteal push your sustained DPS past his burst.
edits.after: First item is even — crit and lifesteal close the gap, but his stun still opens it.

edits.before: This is Renekton's window: with full fury he chains Ruthless Predator (W) stun into Cull the Meek (Q) and Slice/Dice (E) to burst you before your crits scale, so respect his fury bar.
edits.after: This is Renekton's window: above 50 Fury, Ruthless Predator (W) stuns 1.5s instead of 0.75s and destroys damage shields, then Cull the Meek (Q) heals him through the trade. Watch the fury bar, not the cooldown.

edits.before: You spike ahead: with Battle Fury crit chance and lifesteal your sustained DPS overtakes his empowered burst, and once his W stun is on cooldown he can't peel you off.
edits.after: First item is a coin-flip: crit and lifesteal drag your sustained DPS toward his empowered burst, but Ruthless Predator still opens on 16/14/12/10/8s — commit only once that stun is spent.

edits.before: Levels 2 through 5 belong to Renekton: empowered W stun plus Q healing and E mobility let him win every short trade and threaten kills before your crit scaling arrives.
edits.after: Levels 2 and 3 belong to Renekton: an empowered W stun plus Q healing and E mobility win every short trade. By 4-5 it evens out — his fury drains between trades and Bloodlust pays the chip back.

edits.before: From level 6 on you take over — R Undying Rage neutralizes his all-in, and once your first item lands your sustained crit DPS and split-push outclass his fading early power.
edits.after: From level 6 you stabilise — R Undying Rage neutralises his all-in — and by two items your sustained crit DPS and split-push outclass his fading early power. First item is still even.

notes: One thing the mirror already flagged and I could not resolve from data: the Renekton page's diff enum was set to FAV (Renekton favoured) while its own win rate says the opposite. On this side I left diff as FAV — which here reads Tryndamere-favoured, matching 53.12% over 1666 games — and instead brought diffRating and report[14] down to 5/10 so all three header fields agree. If the intended reading is that FAV means the enemy is favoured, this edit is backwards and should be dropped; see questionsForUser.
